# uor-standard-applicability Specification

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json. Change the app through your agent with /prism, not by editing this file. -->

## Purpose

Standard applicability by scope and jurisdiction: Decide whether one candidate standard binds one part of The UOR Foundation, from what the standard's issuer says it covers, whether it is law in a jurisdiction the Foundation is organized or operates in, whether the Foundation carries on the activity the law is conditioned on, whether the Foundation already adopts it, and which facet owns it.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Never applicable when owner is security and inscope is yes

The app SHALL NOT answer `applicable` when owner is security and inscope is yes, because a standard the security facet owns is never claimed by this register.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-001, theorem `inv001Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-001 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `security quoted yes voluntary unbound present no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `applicable`
- **AND** the app answers `secured`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: Always undecided when owner is standards and scope is unread

The app SHALL answer `undecided` when owner is standards and scope is unread, because an unread scope is never decided.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-002, theorem `inv002Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-002 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `standards unread yes voluntary unbound present no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `undecided`
- **AND** the app answers `undecided`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: Always inapplicable when owner is standards and scope is quoted and inscope is yes and force is law and jurisdiction is foreign

The app SHALL answer `inapplicable` when owner is standards and scope is quoted and inscope is yes and force is law and jurisdiction is foreign, because a foreign law does not bind a Colorado nonprofit corporation by organization.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-003, theorem `inv003Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-003 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `standards quoted yes law foreign present no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `inapplicable`
- **AND** the app answers `inapplicable`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: Never inapplicable when owner is standards and scope is quoted and inscope is yes and force is law and jurisdiction is own and activity is undetermined

The app SHALL NOT answer `inapplicable` when owner is standards and scope is quoted and inscope is yes and force is law and jurisdiction is own and activity is undetermined, because a law of the Foundation's jurisdiction whose condition the sources do not settle is never ruled out.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-004, theorem `inv004Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-004 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `standards quoted yes law own undetermined yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `inapplicable`
- **AND** the app answers `conditional`, decided by REQ-006

### Requirement: Always mandatory when owner is standards and scope is quoted and inscope is yes and force is law and jurisdiction is own and activity is present

The app SHALL answer `mandatory` when owner is standards and scope is quoted and inscope is yes and force is law and jurisdiction is own and activity is present, because a law of the Foundation's jurisdiction whose activity it carries on is mandatory.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-005, theorem `inv005Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-005 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `standards quoted yes law own present yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `mandatory`
- **AND** the app answers `mandatory`, decided by REQ-007

### Requirement: REQ-001 secured when owner is security and inscope is yes

The app SHALL answer `secured` when owner is security and inscope is yes, because security/README.md (UOR-Foundation/community@6360c460d56cb225e8ab172fa4d0b6bfc36b78b7) Standards: the security facet models and implements the security and privacy standards; this register only accounts for them.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule1`).

#### Scenario: REQ-001 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `security quoted yes voluntary unbound present no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `secured`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: REQ-002 undecided when scope is unread

The app SHALL answer `undecided` when scope is unread and no earlier rule matches, because AGENTS.md R2 and R4: a scope the issuer's own page did not yield is not restated or guessed; the candidate is carried as an open claim with its URL.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule2`).

#### Scenario: REQ-002 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `standards unread yes voluntary unbound present no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `undecided`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: REQ-003 inapplicable when inscope is no

The app SHALL answer `inapplicable` when inscope is no and no earlier rule matches, because The standard's own scope clause, quoted in standards/snapshot.json, names a subject this part is not.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule3`).

#### Scenario: REQ-003 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `standards quoted no voluntary unbound present yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `inapplicable`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: REQ-004 inapplicable when force is law and jurisdiction is foreign

The app SHALL answer `inapplicable` when force is law and jurisdiction is foreign and no earlier rule matches, because nonprofit/register.json entity (Colorado Secretary of State record 20251193974): The UOR Foundation is a Colorado nonprofit corporation, organized in US-CO under Bylaws 1.1; a law of another jurisdiction does not bind it by organization.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule4`).

#### Scenario: REQ-004 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `standards quoted yes law foreign present no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `inapplicable`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: REQ-005 inapplicable when force is law and activity is absent

The app SHALL answer `inapplicable` when force is law and activity is absent and no earlier rule matches, because The law's own scope clause conditions it on an activity, or a kind of entity, the entity record and the pinned sources show the Foundation is not.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule5`).

#### Scenario: REQ-005 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `standards quoted yes law own absent no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `inapplicable`, decided by REQ-005

### Requirement: REQ-006 conditional when force is law and activity is undetermined

The app SHALL answer `conditional` when force is law and activity is undetermined and no earlier rule matches, because nonprofit/register.json obligations: a conditional obligation whose condition the pinned sources do not settle is undetermined, never assumed away.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule6`).

#### Scenario: REQ-006 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `standards quoted yes law own undetermined yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `conditional`, decided by REQ-006

### Requirement: REQ-007 mandatory when force is law and jurisdiction is own and activity is present

The app SHALL answer `mandatory` when force is law and jurisdiction is own and activity is present and no earlier rule matches, because The law's own scope clause and the entity record: a Colorado nonprofit corporation (Bylaws 1.1) carrying on the activity the law names is bound by it.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule7`).

#### Scenario: REQ-007 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `standards quoted yes law own present yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `mandatory`, decided by REQ-007

### Requirement: REQ-008 adopted when force is voluntary and adopted is yes

The app SHALL answer `adopted` when force is voluntary and adopted is yes and no earlier rule matches, because The citing facet register, standards.lock or the governance register's pinned Foundation document adopts the standard.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule8`).

#### Scenario: REQ-008 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `standards quoted yes voluntary unbound present yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `adopted`, decided by REQ-008

### Requirement: REQ-009 undecided when force is law

The app SHALL answer `undecided` when force is law and no earlier rule matches, because A law whose jurisdiction is not stated as own or foreign is not decided by guess (AGENTS.md R4).

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule9`).

#### Scenario: REQ-009 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `standards quoted yes law unbound present no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `undecided`, decided by REQ-009

### Requirement: Otherwise applicable

The app SHALL answer `applicable` when no rule matches, because The standard's own scope clause covers this part and nothing excludes it: the Foundation's directive is to implement every applicable standard.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: No rule matches

- **WHEN** the request is `standards quoted yes voluntary unbound present no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `applicable`

### Requirement: The first matching rule decides

The app SHALL try REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009 in that order, and the first rule that matches SHALL decide.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: Two rules match

- **WHEN** the request is `standards quoted no voluntary unbound present yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `inapplicable`, decided by REQ-003, the earlier rule

### Requirement: Request and answers

The app SHALL read one request as one line of 7 fields separated by single spaces, in this order, and SHALL answer exactly one of `secured`, `undecided`, `inapplicable`, `conditional`, `mandatory`, `adopted`, `applicable`, or `invalid` for anything else.

| Field | Accepts | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `owner` | `standards`, `security` | the facet that owns the standard: security when the security facet (security/) models it, standards otherwise |
| `scope` | `quoted`, `unread` | quoted when the standard's scope is quoted from its issuer's own page in standards/snapshot.json, or from an authority the nonprofit register pins; unread when the issuer's page could not be read |
| `inscope` | `yes`, `no` | yes when the part is of the subject the standard's scope clause names (organization, nonprofit, process, data, software, webContent, ossProject), as standards/parts.json records the part's subjects |
| `force` | `law`, `voluntary` | law for a statute, a regulation or the official instructions that implement them; voluntary for a standard an organization chooses to adopt |
| `jurisdiction` | `own`, `foreign`, `unbound` | own when the law is of a jurisdiction the entity record places the Foundation in (US, US-CO); foreign for a law of any other jurisdiction; unbound for a voluntary standard, which no jurisdiction enacts |
| `activity` | `present`, `absent`, `undetermined` | whether the Foundation carries on the activity the law's own scope clause conditions it on: present, absent, or undetermined when the pinned sources do not settle it; present for a voluntary standard |
| `adopted` | `yes`, `no` | yes when a facet register, standards.lock or a Foundation document the governance register pins already cites or adopts the standard |

| Answer | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `secured` | Applicable and owned by the security facet, which models and implements it |
| `undecided` | Not decided: the issuer's scope could not be read, so the candidate stays an open claim |
| `inapplicable` | Does not bind this part |
| `conditional` | Law that binds the Foundation once an activity the sources do not settle is carried on; implement it so the condition can be met |
| `mandatory` | Law that binds this part of the Foundation now |
| `adopted` | A voluntary standard in scope that the Foundation already adopts |
| `applicable` | A voluntary standard in scope that the Foundation has not yet adopted |
| `invalid` | the request is malformed |

Verified: reading a request is tested, not proved.

#### Scenario: A malformed request is invalid

- **WHEN** the request is not 7 fields in this order
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `invalid`

## Examples

- `security quoted yes voluntary unbound present no` gives `secured`
- `standards unread yes voluntary unbound present no` gives `undecided`
- `standards quoted no voluntary unbound present yes` gives `inapplicable`
- `standards quoted yes law foreign present no` gives `inapplicable`
- `standards quoted yes law own absent no` gives `inapplicable`
- `standards quoted yes law own undetermined yes` gives `conditional`
- `standards quoted yes law own present yes` gives `mandatory`
- `standards quoted yes voluntary unbound present yes` gives `adopted`
- `standards quoted yes voluntary unbound present no` gives `applicable`
- `standards quoted yes law unbound present no` gives `undecided`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proof is about `judge`, the function the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.
